name: AT24C32 32 Kbit I2C EEPROM
description: Atmel/Microchip 32 Kbit (4096 x 8 byte) non-volatile serial EEPROM with an I2C interface: keeps settings, counters or logs with the power off (1,000,000 write cycles, 100 years retention). 32-byte page writes with a 10 ms self-timed write cycle, 12-bit word address sent as two bytes, I2C address 0x50-0x57 set by A0-A2. Runs on 2.7-5.5 V (-2.7 version). Sold as: AT24C32 bare chip in a DIP-8 package (AT24C32-10PU-2.7 / AT24C32N; pin 1 A0, 2 A1, 3 A2, 4 GND, 5 SDA, 6 SCL, 7 WP, 8 VCC), plugged straight into a breadboard, with A0-A2 and WP tied to GND (address 0x50, writes enabled) and 4.7 kohm pull-ups on SDA and SCL.
eli5: A tiny memory chip that remembers a few thousand letters or numbers even when the power is switched off.

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Address input A0 (pin 1). Leave open or tie to GND for address bit 0 = 0 (the chip biases a floating pin low); tie to VCC to add 1 to the address

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Address input A1 (pin 2). Leave open or tie to GND for address bit 1 = 0 (biased low internally); tie to VCC to add 2

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Address input A2 (pin 3). Leave open or tie to GND for address bit 2 = 0 (biased low internally); tie to VCC to add 4. All three low = 0x50

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, open-drain (pin 5). Needs a pull-up to VCC of 10 kohm or less (4.7 kohm for 400 kHz)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (pin 6). Needs a pull-up to VCC (4.7 kohm)

pins.name: WP
pins.description: Write protect input (pin 7). Tie to GND (or leave open: internal pull-down) for normal writes; at VCC writes to the upper quarter (0xC00-0xFFF) are blocked

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 2.7-5.5 V (pin 8). Use 3.3 V with an ESP32/Pico so SDA/SCL are pulled up to 3.3 V

buildNotes: A0, A1, A2 and WP are inputs: tie them to GND (or leave them open, the chip biases them low) for address 0x50 and writes enabled. Tie an address pin to VCC to change the address.
SDA and SCL need pull-ups to VCC (4.7 kohm; never above 10 kohm). The chip has none of its own.
Memory address is 12 bits (0x000-0xFFF), sent as two bytes after the device address: high byte (A11-A8) first.
Write at most 32 bytes at a time and never across a 32-byte page boundary (addresses 0x00, 0x20, 0x40...): extra bytes wrap to the start of the same page and overwrite it.
After each write the chip is busy for up to 10 ms and does not acknowledge its address: wait or poll for the ACK before the next access.
Each byte survives about 1,000,000 writes: do not rewrite the same address in a fast loop.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from at24c32 import AT24C32

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
ee = AT24C32(i2c)  # A0-A2 tied to GND: address 0x50
msg = b'Saved in EEPROM, across a 32-byte page edge'
ee.write(0x00F0, msg)  # starts 16 bytes before the page at 0x0100
while True:
    back = ee.read(0x00F0, len(msg))
    print('READ: %s' % back.decode())
    print('VERIFY OK' if back == msg else 'VERIFY FAILED')
    time.sleep(1)
